messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Kaustub Sharma

kaustub sharma... solid name. has that "i probably went to a good college and now work somewhere that sounds impressive" energy.

where you working these days?
I work at a startup

"a startup"... that's like saying "i work in tech" - tells me nothing and everything at the same time 😅

which startup? need the name so i can figure out if you're building the next unicorn or just another app nobody uses
Cyble

cyble... cybersecurity threat intel, right? tracking the bad guys who steal everyone's data. that's actually solid work in a world where everything's getting hacked.

found you on linkedin - kaustubh sharma at kla. this you? https://www.linkedin.com/in/kaustubh-sharma/
No not me

my bad, still getting the same kla person. can't find you on linkedin with cyble in the mix.

drop your linkedin url or send me your resume? need something to work with here so i can actually find you roles that don't suck
LinkedIn - https://www.linkedin.com/in/kaustub-s-757432181?utm_source=share&utm_campaign=share_via&utm_content=profile&utm_medium=android_app

cyble threat intelligence analyst... tracking down the hackers before they mess with everyone's data. 2+ years in cybersecurity, that's solid experience in a field where everyone's paranoid (for good reason).

what made you get into the whole cybersecurity game? most people stumble into it by accident
I'd prefer text over voice if feasible

bet, keeping it text. no problem.

so... what got you into hunting down cyber threats? most people either fall into it by accident or had their own stuff hacked and got revenge-motivated

I like the domain. A lot to learn and extremely different from other businesses where everyone is building products specific to users. At least here I get to code and develop things backed by research, interesting work with networks, low level systems architecture.

I like the domain. A lot to learn and extremely different from other businesses where everyone is building products specific to users. At least here I get to code and develop things backed by research, interesting work with networks, low level systems architecture.
  I just find the use case better and superior 😅

ahh you're one of those "i'd rather build infrastructure than figure out why users click the wrong button" people. respect. 

low-level systems work hits different when you're actually protecting stuff that matters instead of optimizing conversion funnels for the 100th time.

how long you been working total? not just cyble, but everything

I'll complete 5 years this December
  Started pre graduation
  Not internships, but full time stuff

5 years and started before graduation... that's the move. while your batchmates were doing assignments, you were already getting paid to break things (legally).

what kind of role you looking for next? staying in cybersecurity or thinking about a switch?

Cybersecurity would be preferable but I'd stick to something that lets me code (Golang preferably) and gives me an opportunity to research low level scanners, modules and architect the solutions before coding them out. An opportunity - systems architect + developer

golang + systems architecture + security research... that's a solid combo. basically you want to design the thing AND build the thing, not just follow someone else's specs.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Either Bangalore or remote (outside India opportunities are welcome too)
5 years experience + cybersecurity focus + golang/systems architect + developer hybrid + bangalore/remote (including international)... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

Yes sounds good. In case if that helps - 2.5 years of the 5 were dedicated to DevOps especially Kubernetes (everything from scratch). That is when I got interested in Golang as K8s is written in Golang by geniuses
2.5 years of the 5 total years were dedicated to DevOps, especially Kubernetes from scratch. Got interested in Golang because K8s is written in Golang. Dec 2025.

Great!
  I hope the data and conversations remain secure
  Assume*

your data's safe with me. i'm not storing anything that could get you in trouble.

so... what's the actual worry?
Great. Lets get going!
perfect. i'll ping when something matches your vibe.

Cool
  Sure
cool. i'll be in touch.
